newsitem.title: USA: Memo group to resume aluminum data publication.
newsitem.headline: Memo group to resume aluminum data publication.

text.p: The Memorandum of Understanding's working group is to resume publishing production and trade data for Russia and other signatory countries of the now expired two-year inter-governmental agreement which curbed aluminum production in 1994 and 1995.
Publication was suspended when the MOU expired early 1996.

Patricia Plunkert of the U.S. Geological Survey and U.S. member of the MOU working group, said publication of data on primary aluminum production, imports and exports on a monthly basis will resume in August, or even as early as July.
"It should help the market," Plunkert said.
The data will go back two years from the first month published.
At present Russian production is merged with the International Primary Aluminium Institute's (IPAI) monthly data for the Europe.
The signatories to the MOU were Norway, Australia, U.S., Canada, Russia and the European Union.
However, Russia will probably supply export and import volumes on a quarterly basis, Plunkert said.
The MOU was an intergovernmental response to plummeting alumium prices amid soaring Russian exports, but drew criticism from U.S. consumers.

The agreement prompted a U.S. Justice probe into possible anti-competitive practices by domestic producers who curbed output. Justice confirmed last month that the probe was now dropped, with no action taken.
